Our first market is Portugal, where we are anchoring an EU STEP-funded sovereign 5G manufacturing and deployment programme in partnership with ANACOM. Portugal is set to be the reference architecture for an EU-aligned global private network platform.

We serve logistics operators, manufacturers, ports, and critical national infrastructure. Our target customers are multinationals who need one private 5G contract that works everywhere they operate.
The private 5G market is growing at 40%+ CAGR toward $23B by 2030. Lyrebird is the only company positioned to capture it at a global, licensed, sovereign scale.

We are growing fast and hiring exceptional 5G engineers, network operators, and commercial leaders. If you want to build something that has never been built so join us.

Name: Bunce
Description:
It’s hard to be thousands of miles away from the people you care about. But it shouldn’t be hard to get it touch with them. We believe strongly in our commitment to connecting family, friends and loved ones by delivering small value transfers across the globe, because even a little means a lot! 

Bunce was founded to help families stay connected. On an individual basis this is clearly great for the people and families sending money, but imagine communities, or even countries coming together, and the cumulative effect could be a defining moment.

We might just be helping people build a better world.


How, you ask?

Well we recognise that the way people use money is changing. Millions of us now rely on Mobile Money services instead of bank accounts, so we offer transfers directly to them.

By providing a simple way to top-up anyone’s mobile phone, any network and at any time, instantly, we believe we have made a great start towards our mission to “Bring your loved ones closer”. We are connected to over 400 network operations in 130 countries, but we won’t stop there. 

Access to phone credit is only the beginning towards our broader vison to provide useful and affordable financial services and products. An estimated 2 billion working-age adults – more than half of the world’s total adult population – do not have access to financial services. At Bunce our financial inclusion efforts seek to ensure that all communities, regardless of income level, have access to and can effectively use financial services they need to improve their lives.

‘Bunce’ is an old English term meaning ‘unexpected benefit, luck or windfall’. We want our customers to experience exactly this. And because we understand the importance of staying connected, this is only the first step. 

 We want to empower families and communities around the world, from being able to facilitate day to day living to long term goals to cater for unexpected emergencies.

We will be launching some fantastic products over the next few months. Join us on our journey of making this world a better, caring and connected global community.


Bunce.
Caring.
Convenient.
Connected.

Name: Digital Places
Description:
Digital Places is a collaborative membership programme established by and for local authorities to address mobile connectivity challenges, delivering better connectivity for residents, businesses and public services.

At the heart of the programme is a data-driven model that combines crowdsourced data with field measurements to build a real-world picture of where connectivity problems exist and why. The model does not simply identify where signal is poor, it assesses how important those gaps are, cross-referencing connectivity data with population, infrastructure and socioeconomic metrics to ensure every intervention is prioritised according to local need.

The programme provides a structured pathway from evidence gathering through to delivery. It develops practical plans supported by commercial insight and procurement guidance, engages directly with mobile network operators and solutions providers, and manages implementation through to impact reporting.

By bringing multiple local authorities together under a standardised, collaborative model, Digital Places creates the scale to lower costs, reduce duplication and drive the market influence needed to attract meaningful operator investment. Members benefit from shared tools, tested delivery mechanisms and a collective voice that shifts engagement with the market from isolated local challenges toward coordinated, investment-ready opportunities.

Digital Places, giving a local voice to connectivity improvement.

It will enable the participating countries to increase access to quality and affordable Information and Communication Technology (ICT) services. 

The SVG project which is 100 percent financed from the World Bank through a credit facility would be implemented over a 5-year period. It is estimated to cost US$6.0 million or EC$16.0 million. The year 2005 saw another milestone as the Connections Centres chain of seven retail stores, along with their corporate team, merged with Get Connected through acquisition.

This setup underscores its position as the largest privately owned mobile phone retailer in the UK, with a wealth of experience exceeding 30 years in connecting people through major telecommunications service providers.

Name: insightteleconsult ltd
Description:
InsightTeleConsult (ITC) is a UK telecoms consultancy built on many decades of BT and Openreach operational experience. We support organisations preparing for the PSTN switch-off and assessing the practical impacts of Openreach’s expanding Exchange Exit programme. Our background spans field engineering, service delivery, copper network operations, network operations management, civils delivery, PIA planning, power resilience, Redcare, OSS/BSS alignment and the operational realities of maintaining, migrating and retiring the UK’s network infrastructure.

To meet the scale of the national programme, ITC has established a pre-emptive Exchange Exit Team. Formed ahead of market demand, this group brings together senior ex-BT/Openreach specialists with experience across network operations, migration planning, NGA platform transitions, civils programme leadership, PIA route assessment, legacy copper engineering, monitored service transitions and power resilience across exchange and network environments.

This capability allows us to identify risks long before exit notices appear, including copper and analogue dependencies, platform and service impacts, civils constraints, PIA route considerations, resilience and power issues, undocumented routing paths, OSS/BSS gaps and operational migration challenges. We believe Exchange Exit will define the next decade of UK telecoms operations, and our team is positioned to support organisations through this transition with practical, grounded insight.

Areas of expertise: PSTN Switch-Off (2027), Exchange Exit Readiness, Network Operations & Migration Management, NGA Platform Migration, Civils & Infrastructure Advisory, PIA Planning, Power & Resilience Assessment, Redcare/Monitored Service Impact, Copper Dependency Mapping, OSS/BSS Alignment.
If PSTN switch-off or Exchange Exit is on your radar, we’re happy to talk — no obligation. Honest, practical insight from ex-Openreach and BT people.

Fibeo is building a fundamentally different kind of broadband company in the United Kingdom.

For decades, the sector has operated on the same model. Customers pay monthly bills while ownership, control and long term value sit with a small group of external shareholders. The incentives are clear, and so are the outcomes. Rising prices, complex structures and limited accountability.

Investment is focused only where it strengthens network quality, resilience and customer experience. Governance and remuneration prioritise sustainable value creation over short term gain.

Fibeo will launch publicly in Autumn 2026. Ahead of launch, we will open an investment campaign to support our next phase of growth and invite aligned supporters to participate. An exclusive pre launch event will take place prior to rollout, formally introducing the business and its long term vision. Priority service access will be offered to early registrants.

What is SentryPeer?

SentryPeer is designed to help detect compromised VoIP accounts. These credentials could have been gathered from desk phones, softphones, PBXs and WebRTC services for example. It works by your system always sending us an API call for each phone call (or IP address) you want to check. We then send you back a response with the results of our analysis.
